entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Ḥamza ibn al-Ḥasan ibn al-Mū'addib al-Iṣbahānī Abū ‘Abd Allāh, commonly known as Ḥamza al-Iṣfahānī or Hamza Esfahani, was a Persian philologist and historian, who wrote in Arabic during the 'Abbasid and Buyid eras. He spent most of his life in his native town, Isfahan, and visited Baghdad at least three times during his lifetime. He had contact with many important scholars and historians, among them al-Tabari and Ibn Durayd. He wrote a history of Isfahan, a famous chronology of pre-Islamic and Islamic dynasties known as Taʾrīk̲h̲ sinī mulūk al-arḍ wa ’l-anbiyāʾ, and some other works on lexicography and poetry.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a Persian philologist and historian, Hamza al-Isbahani's works on lexicography and poetry contributed to the development of Arabic literature. His chronology of pre-Islamic and Islamic dynasties provides valuable insights into the historical context of Isfahan during the 'Abbasid and Buyid eras.
